newsitem.title: INDIA: India bullion pulled down by world trends.
newsitem.headline: India bullion pulled down by world trends.

** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.64 gramme) opened 200 rupees lower at 52,600 rupees per piece after losing 200 rupees on Tuesday.
** Silver (.999) opened 105 rupees lower at 6,325 rupees per kg as sharp losses in the world market triggered hectic selling.

Gold 24 carat opened 15 rupees lower at 4,500 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,515 rupees on the back of fresh selling influenced by a setback in the world market, dealers said on Wednesday.
Gold was down by 15 rupees on Tuesday.
"Sluggish seasonal buying also weakened market sentiment while the premiums for import licences for bullion rose to 13.25 percent from 13.10/13.15 percent," one broker said.
"Festivals are round the corner but buyers kept to the sidelines expecting further price erosion in gold," he added.
Meanwhile prices of a gold biscuit (116.64 gramme) opened 200 rupees lower at 52,600 rupees per piece after losing 200 rupees on Tuesday.

Silver (.999) crashed by 105 rupees in early trade at 6,325 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,430 rupees on the back of sharp losses in the world market which prompted heavy unloading by local stockists. Silver was up by 30 rupees per kg on Tuesday.
